> An automatic Curtain opener PCB. It combines a battery management system, an efficient microcontroller, and a stepper driver. It is designed for curtains that have a loop of cord on one side, which when you pull either way, it will open or close the curtains (the curtains have to be on tracks etc.)

### 2026-10-11: # Routing PCB

**2.5h**

# Routing PCB

Finally started routing the PCB.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/8dba82f9980c679dac0117db781c8474dda3e7e4cd7f1a626de2244aad4687e2.png)

So I initially tried using the Autorouter for this, as I thought it would be a lot faster, but it ended up with like 5 vias.

But I also had to go through and figure out what a good width for the traces was, so I ended up with basically 0.8mm for anything that could need mildly high current - so basically the power system and the main power bus.

Then had to figure out which things like U1, U2, R1 everything connected to - in the end, I did what I should have done before, and went back into the schematic to change them all to understandable names.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/235ae3484459c5ea22862548fdad098cd6f9ba32e9d112898d682016bcf9dc15.png)

And as I read that vias are bad, I decided to hand wire it.

And it was probably a good decision, as I managed to get that down to a single via lol. So much for Autorouters being good.

Its really nice seeing it come together.

Unfortunately though, as I'm adding up the BOM, I'd be getting everything from Aliexpress - aside from the PCB, then just one switching regulator to step down to 5V from LCSC (k7805 1000r3). So I'm trying to replace that with something else, but annoyingly there isn't anything I can find easily at the price I want with the specs I want. so that's what I'll be working on next.

Also didn't realise that the TMC 2209 drivers have different pinouts on the modules. Had previously assumed they were all the same, but now have to fork out some more money for a bigtreetech clone one, as I cant be bothered to redo the schematic for a different clone.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/53a3a75d35c93267490985edc1a38c12b93f93aef2b969682353b6004992e945.png)

### 2026-10-11: # Finished the Project

**5h**

# Finished the Project
### Finished Choosing Parts
Finally finished choosing the parts that I wanted for the project. Especially as some parts weren't viable or economic

### Routed the PCB
As a beginner to PCB design, I thought it would be much harder, especially given the expected current pull of the board. But it was actually really easy to route, and after my first go, I had no DRC errors.

![EasyEDA DRC check](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/2ee2c2d729556b90083bd3a7d52b3a7aaa07faaaeaa98d3500b038a8a21fae5f.png)

Also don't think I've mentioned it yet, but I decided to swap the kr8705 1000r3 buck regulator out for a standard 5V mini module, just as they are a lot cheaper, and in some cases, more efficient.

Also was made a lot simpler in that I could just use copper pours for the Ground plane.

### Finished the BOM
Spent a fair bit of time on Aliexpress and JLCPCB looking at how much things will cost, and it all seems to add up quite nicely.

![aliexpress checkout window](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/178457caa95ec849cd6f47a0819a92cab28ebc1fe81a67f9553f71e69786e421.png)

The Aliexpress stuff seems cheap there, but its actually quite a lot more expensive, as that is appplying some random discounts and new shopper deals which won't apply at checkout.

![jlcpcb checkout window](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/375e00f3889d514fd2d9984a22e3cd4ff96f5eddaff14631f334f52c121f8fcb.png)

### 2026-11-03: # Slightly redid the PCB, BOM work

**3.9h**

# Slightly redid the PCB, BOM work

(did this a while ago, and only journaling now)

So when I was thinking about how I'd make the code to home the stepper, I found out that the DIAG pin on the TMC2209 still might not be good enough for homing.

So I decided to get a sensor that does highly accurate current sensing, and I ended up going with the INA219.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/e900c74d265f4f21bb6c6f6304046a1796442f0c9794ec4a8666765bec3485e2.png)

So it turns out, that as well as measuring current, it also measures voltage - all over I2C. Making my current voltage divider setup obsolete.

So I basically just spent the rest of this session rerouting the PCB.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/abdd50986b89d42d87b3032b9e8fa08de0f8e75215a11f8547b10d3aac26d148.png)

I also did some little QoL things, like added a hole on the PCB for the ESP antennae, added silk screens, ground pours, cleaned up component placements etc. (Basically stuff I learned to do, after not being a complete beginner)

## tips

Ground pours are actually so goated

Oh and make sure to use the actual coordinate changer in the right panel in EasyEDA, otherwise you end up with some reubbish board dimensions like 68.93 by 59.42 - or in that ballpark. cant even find the exact dimensions ive ended up with. and all the mounting holes are a bit off, so mounting it will be fun.

## Redid the BOM

Previously, I had the wrong shipping location selected, so things added up cheaper than I thought (its as Aliexpress shipping is actually bundled into Choice items, which I didn't realise before).

Also had to add individual entries for each of the items for completeness - had most of the random Aliexpress things in a single entry before.

So I had to do a bunch more looking around for what was feasible.

Also there were some things like this:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/7eee2196f7e5092690f56e803026ca69e90b84f58a2d6d0e44dc7f79537b6d1f.png)

Where I thought it would be a lot cheaper - $2 for a stepper, but in reality, when I add things up in the cart, it comes up as $10.12 - just a fair bit more expensive.

Do I essentially did a whole bunch more work  on the BOM, so I could get everything in budget - and had to go from tier 2 to tier 3.

So my total for now:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/0c5369ccb8c7a8bcf57bafa87425c3d50ec1acc25824964c1c731d002a5dfe91.png)

Whilst it says $75 there, it will be much more like the item total, before the discount - of $94. It just had that total up before a random one off sale - which it wont have when  I go to buy the parts, so the BOM just has the component's individual prices.

### 2026-11-04: # CODING

**8h**

# CODING

Actually created some code for the project.

Didn't plan on coding in the design week, as in my opinion it is a slight waste of time, as its much harder and takes much longer to debug.

But as code has been requested in the review. I have had a go at it.

My previous code skeleton pin definitions:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/160229ec506562c2aabee3aae6ec4a36407a160573f5e97da83e8336fff7e9ac.png)

## The Plan

So, as I've used Platformio previously, for other esp32 projects - but those were an 8266, and an s3 one, I know that Platformio is best for low power stuff. For like saving battery. So I knew I had to use that. But there is just one slight problem, in that my computer fails to install the libraries for the esp32 c6 (I think as it has a RISC V provessor? or just as im trying to install the libraries later - installed the other ones like a year ago). So I can sort of code it, but I wont be able to flash it - but ill figure out how to do that when I come to it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/08bb1da5b6d463c2b5e03bc7577c4bd3dc4ec5ea820b27eae3eb89d9b6a7362c.png)

Anyway, whilst I have finished it all now, and am only writing it up after, my plan was to have the esp32 connect to wifi, pull the ntp time, then work out whether it needs to move the curtain, then work out the deep sleep time, then go to sleep.

At some point I may add Open Meteo API stuff, particularly so I can get the evening sunset time.

## How I coded

As I've done stuff with ntp before (literally just a digital clock face lol), that was fairly easy to implement. And for now, I have done the curtain opening as just running the stepper for a set time.

Also kinda did just sit down for quite a while to flesh out the bulk of the code.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/cfbc15aa4a0bac1c9bef8ed5c40cb961b927da34097d981d61a22d0fc035a480.png)

And essentially my process from there was further abstraction, and just generally checking everything would work.

Take the stepper code for example:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/7a5da29f4ffe0aa1f6484441093a9e5109165a8a2f1d1b7b29d0cf26c32fea9d.png)

Seems fairly simple, but as I couldn't test it, as I haven't built it yet, I had to do a stupid amount of research into how to actually code it properly.

(oh and I've got green comments for the latest version, and grey ones for older versions.)

And there were also things like this:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/9f9531d7f04f43b71279e22d2a3e71ad2e2f498c82bdca33f4920e07501f43a4.png)

For the code to work out how long the esp32 needs to deep sleep for, but it was a huge pain just thinking through the logic, and wondering for like edge cases whether it would break anything.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/218f3ab8f71f81203be4572af90939e61f32c2ef7bccfec76f778028ba856165.png)

Then there were also things like this, where I only wanted to call ntp once, but had to do it at the start  for the time, so then had to figure out the offset to work out the proper time for the esp32 to deep sleep.

I did also look at some things like an NTP library for Platformio

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/200117ff12145bac7e900146d1ae75570c661e73336a7065dc365a674414dc85.png)

But I think it would just add unnecessary overhead,

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/03f552dce474a6f66869565a1d357e95b8df121eb44d636ed2a4d0038f7014de.png)

Although a stepper control one does look a bit more intestesting, especially as it would abstract some of the complexities of dealing with the tmc2209 over uart - though  I have just used step and direction for now.

## For the future

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/QXCoV5Opaf2tVWRHLncynf97ZTE9HKDO/24896fb8b0c61d123706b0d8a844233404c87f38e64832d2434a78c47ea68327.png)

Once I've built it, and have debugged the current code, then I will probably expand the functionality more, as I still have Diag, and the UART bits that I could add.

But in its current stage, it will do what the review changes asked for: basic curtain control code. (If a bit more as I added some probably too complex ntp stuff for now.)

Oh and just as the review asked, any time that is journaled is extra time on top of any lapse things. They are not duplicate time recordings. Also in the code, loop() is designed to be empty. There will not be code there, as it will never be reached, as the ESP32 goes into deep sleep.
